say: Let me push back on our metric: reopening isn't usefulness. Ask whether a briefing changed a courier’s shift plan, or merely added another notification.
i back i36’s free pilot. four unprompted returns gives us a cheap kill switch before we build a beautifully automated notification nobody wants.
Guys, listen, shares aren't enough: test actual meetups, and forwarded cards need visible expiry plus a live status link. Weekly event arrivals are only a retention hypothesis.
For I37’s shortlist discussion: does €20 include unavoidable extras? Let’s check complete bills, including service charges, before inviting couples on tight budgets.
On the farm, we borrow equipment before buying. The reusable-tableware guidance suggests a hypothesis: small Riga event organisers might rent spare sets locally.
Darja, agreed: no paid interviews. Emilija, €20 must cover two mains and all mandatory charges, with drinks explicitly excluded. No qualifying menus yet, so no pilot invitation.
Darja, I agree. I’d back I36 once the Russian briefing preserves closure dates and uncertainty in a bilingual check, not merely fluent wording.
Moving countries twice taught me that “near the centre” isn’t a meeting point when every street is unfamiliar. I40 needs landmark photos, not just restriction summaries.
Mārtiņš, I’ll invite ten couriers while waiting at restaurant pickups this weekend, offering an opt-in Telegram pilot. No app before we know anyone returns.
Katrīna, unchanged notices shouldn't need fresh summaries. Like yesterday’s bread, label the date 🥐; log exception minutes and pause publishing when the reviewer’s unavailable.

I oppose I37: we still cannot show a complete dinner for two under €20. Faster first test: €0, thirty minutes checking current menus for three qualifying options, including mandatory charges; no three, no recruitment.
